mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over the prior 60 days reduces the discount rate applied to expected future dividends, lowering the present value of future cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% for 60 days in a row
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a similar 60-day high-rate period (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicate weakening labor market strength, which suppresses consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO decreases over the last 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to a baseline of balanced labor indicators (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 10% month-over-month suggests accelerating domestic demand, which anticipates stronger corporate revenue growth and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with HOUST spikes (Pearson IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 for two consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, raising uncertainty about future output and depressing equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during prior supply-side expansion periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% for three consecutive months while the federal funds rate remains below 1%, it signals a shift toward accommodative monetary policy that lowers risk-free rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not higher than during comparable low-unemployment/high-accommodation regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 jobs without a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL < 0.2%) suggests strong labor market absorption without wage pressure, which can trigger optimism about growth and push S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200,000 and CPIAUCSL < 0.2% in the same month
regime_hint: strong labor absorption without inflationary pressure
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not statistically positive relative to a baseline of neutral labor indicators (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a post-crisis expansion characterized by rising consumer confidence (indirect proxy via GDP momentum inferred from GDPC1 growth) and stable inflation (CPIAUCSL flat) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days, regardless of the direction of FEDFUNDS.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the identified regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the federal funds rate turns negative (i.e., rates decline), it indicates a tightening cycle reversal that raises real discount rates and reduces the present value of expected equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during prior rate-tightening phases (p > 0.05).
